name: Zendesk help center entry point (public, unauthenticated)
tier_rationale: Established company with published terms, a privacy policy and a business offering (A8 trusted); P371 provider_tier 'trusted' (council #1).

reliability.justification: First-party answer of the requested <name>.zendesk.com help center; an agent-only account without a public help center cannot be told apart without login endpoints (rule 2), so 'absent' means 'no public help center under this name'. A name never proves which organisation owns the account (P371 FC5).

help_center.title: Zendesk tenant discovery: https://<name>.zendesk.com/hc with redirects not followed (200 or 301 to the same host /hc/<locale> = help center exists; 404 help-center 'Not Found' or 301 to help-center-closed = no public help center)
help_center.notes: Research C0797, live 2026-11-26 (batch p3-G13-1): on the fixed path /hc support.zendesk.com answered 301 to https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us and a random name answered 404 'Not Found' with header zendesk-service: help-center; the research saw the help-center-closed redirect on '/' only (both marker sets are read, see docs/backlog/p3-G13-1.md). A random name on /hc/en-us got a Cloudflare managed challenge (cf-mitigated: challenge): challenges stop the vendor check for the run and are never retried or bypassed (A9). Login redirects (/access/..., /signin) are never followed (rule 2). Politeness budget (not published by Zendesk): 0.5 request/s and 60 per day per egress, one GET per candidate, no retries.

notes: Owned by batch p3-G13-1 (P371, module saas_tenant_discovery). Only the fixed FC2 path is ever built and redirects are never followed; the candidate name is the only value Zendesk receives.
